title: Sanitization playbook for async shard migration leak that caused cross-tenant KV growth
creator: Daniel Kim
description: Summary: A production incident on 2025-02-08 revealed sustained memory growth in the KV/prefix cache on a subset of shards after an async shard migration path completed. Growth manifested as slow eviction (eviction stalls) and occasional tenant-visible 5xxs when background compaction raced with re-insert logic. Root cause analysis pointed to a race where tombstoned prefix entries could be resurrected by an async migration callback, bypassing usual reference-count checks and leaving orphaned payloads and index entries. This ticket is the engineering playbook and action plan to sanitize survivors, prevent recurrence, and add targeted telemetry and automated remediation.
timeline: 2025-02-08 01:14 UTC: First alert — increase in host RSS and eviction latency on pool-g-4
2025-02-08 01:22 UTC: Pager escalated; on-call triage suspected eviction storm
2025-02-08 02:05 UTC: Narrowed to async shard migration waveform after correlating bump with migration job IDs
2025-02-08 04:40 UTC: Hotfix — disable async-merge path on affected region; mem growth stopped but orphan entries remained
2025-02-09 to 2025-02-13: Offline heap sampling and lead engineer investigation; reproduced race in stress harness
2025-02-14: Drafted remediation design and initial PR: add resurrection guard + sanitization sweep
2025-02-18: Canary rollout of sanitization sweep on low-traffic tenant; no regressions observed
2025-02-25: This ticket created to track follow-ups and full rollout
root_cause: A race in the async shard migration callback path allowed tombstoned prefix entries to be re-inserted without updating the canonical reference-count and checksum checks. The migration callback was executed on a worker thread that interleaved with the compaction/eviction thread, and a short window allowed a stale pointer to be promoted back into the active index. That promotion kept large payload buffers alive while the index thought the entry was removed, causing gradual heap growth and eviction thrashing.
impact_summary: Affected ~12% of KV-serving hosts in the region for ~18 hours. Resulted in increased p95 token latency for a subset of customers and 5 small incidents with transient 5xx for high-throughput tenants. No data corruption at application level, but internal index budget was exceeded and some background jobs were starved.
detection: Existing alerts detected host RSS and eviction latency but did not surface the migration correlation. Added steps include linking migration job IDs in allocation traces and emitting a short-lived 'migration-resurrection' counter when a migration callback attempts to recreate a tombstone key.
mitigation_steps: Hotfix: disable async-merge path for migration jobs (rolled back safely once sweep verified)
Immediate: run a one-off sanitization sweep that verifies reference counts against live payloads and frees orphan buffers
Operational: increase eviction aggressiveness on affected pools for 24h after migration rollouts
Customer-facing: notified SRE and CS for high-throughput tenants with timeline and mitigation steps
action_items: ENG-834999-A1: Add resurrection-guard in migration callback (idempotent insert path) — owners: Priya, Miguel — estimate 3
ENG-834999-A2: Implement periodic sanitization sweep with low-cpu budget and safety-first free logic — owners: Daniel, Asha — estimate 3
ENG-834999-A3: Emit migration-associated telemetry (migration_job_id in allocation traces) and add metric 'kvcache.migration.resurrect_attempt' — owner: Observability team — estimate 2
ENG-834999-A4: Backfill heap-sample dashboard tiles and create alert for 'orphan_payload_count > 1000' per host — owner: Reliability — estimate 2
ENG-834999-A5: Add unit+stress tests that fuzz interleaving between migration callback and compaction thread — owner: Eng QA — estimate 2
ENG-834999-A6: Run a global audit runbook and confirm no active orphan count across fleets before re-enabling async-merge — owners: SRE + Eng — estimate 1
decisions: Do not pursue immediate schema changes to index format; prefer a code-level guard and sanitization sweep to minimize rollout blast radius
Expose migration_job_id in existing trace/span metadata to accelerate future correlation rather than inventing a new tracing pipeline
Make the sanitization sweep conservative by default (dry-run mode) and enable force-free only under SRE approval
final_resolution: Merged resurrection-guard and sanitization sweep. Performed staged rollout and validated via canary tenant and targeted heap-sampling. Re-enabled async-merge only after zero orphan payloads observed on canary hosts and SRE sign-off. Added alerts and tracing to prevent repeat.
follow_up_notes: Consider formalizing a 'migration safety checklist' for future async features that mutate index state
Schedule a 90-minute post-implementation review with Design/PM to evaluate UX of runbook automation
Evaluate whether reference-count semantics should be part of the public KV cache API contract to avoid future accidental bypasses
